questions.q: In the United States, which is the most common unit for comparing energy sources or fuels?
questions.explain: Converting fuels to a common unit lets you compare them directly.
questions.evidence: In the United States, Btu is the most common unit for comparing energy sources or fuels.

questions.q: Which of these is energy conservation rather than energy efficiency?
options: Turning lights off when they are not needed
questions.explain: Efficiency does the same job with less energy; conservation avoids using energy at all.
questions.evidence: installing energy-efficient lights is an efficiency measure, and turning lights off when not needed, either manually or with timers or motion sensor switches, is conservation.

questions.q: Why is electricity called a secondary energy source?
options: It is produced by converting primary sources such as coal, gas, nuclear, solar and wind
It is less important than oil
It is always produced second, after heat
It can only be stored in batteries
questions.explain: The losses of that conversion are part of why saving electricity matters.
questions.evidence: The electricity we use is a secondary energy source because it is produced by converting primary sources of energy such as coal, natural gas, nuclear energy, solar energy, and wind energy into electrical power.

questions.q: Which home energy uses continue all year round?
questions.explain: Heating and cooling are seasonal; these uses are constant.
questions.evidence: Water heating, lighting, and refrigeration are year-round home energy uses.

questions.q: What is manufacturing, as an energy-using industrial activity?
options: The physical, mechanical or chemical transformation of materials into new products
questions.explain: Industry also includes agriculture, mining and construction.
questions.evidence: Manufacturing is the physical, mechanical, or chemical transformation of materials or substances into new products.

questions.q: What is the UK Energy Savings Opportunity Scheme (ESOS)?
options: A voluntary green label for products
A mandatory energy assessment scheme for UK organisations that meet the qualification criteria
questions.explain: Qualifying organisations must assess their energy use and report opportunities.
questions.evidence: is a mandatory energy assessment scheme for organisations in the UK that meet the qualification criteria.

questions.q: What is an ESOS assessment designed to identify?
options: Tailored, cost-effective measures to save energy and achieve carbon and cost savings
Which staff use the most electricity
questions.explain: The audit points to savings that make business sense.
questions.evidence: The ESOS assessment is designed to identify tailored and cost-effective measures that allow participating businesses to save energy and achieve carbon and cost savings.

questions.q: What is 'de minimis' energy consumption under ESOS?
options: The maximum 5% of total energy consumption that may be excluded from audits
The smallest site in the organisation
questions.explain: At least 95% of energy use must be covered by audits or another compliance route.
questions.evidence: The maximum 5% of total energy consumption that may be excluded from any audit or alternative compliance measures is known as your ‘de minimis’ energy consumption.

questions.q: How must an energy intensity ratio be expressed?
options: As a percentage of the energy bill
In kWh per unit of an activity indicator, for example kWh/m² of floor area
As the number of energy audits per year
questions.explain: Ratios let you compare energy use as an organisation grows or shrinks.
questions.evidence: The units for any energy intensity ratio must be expressed in kWh /x

questions.q: If verifiable data for an indicator is not available, what should you do?
options: Leave the indicator out of the audit
Copy last year's figure without explanation
Ask the regulator for an exemption
Use a reasonable estimate and record the estimation method in your evidence pack
questions.explain: Methods include direct comparison, pro-rata extrapolation and benchmarking.
questions.evidence: If verifiable data is not available, you should use a reasonable estimate and keep a record of the method used to estimate the indicator in your evidence pack.

questions.q: If energy data is not in your accounting system, what does the guidance suggest?
options: Nominate a person to record energy use and costs
Stop monitoring energy until the system is upgraded
Rely on the supplier's marketing data
questions.explain: Reliable monitoring is the foundation of any energy audit.
questions.evidence: If the data is not included in your accounting system, nominate a person to record energy use and costs.

questions.q: What should investment, equipment replacement and maintenance decisions consider?
options: Only the energy saved in the first month
The full cost to the organisation
questions.explain: Life-cycle cost analysis compares options over their whole working life.
questions.evidence: It is helpful to ensure that investment decisions and equipment replacement or maintenance decisions consider the full cost to the organisation.

questions.q: Which unit is normally used to measure electricity?
questions.explain: Barrels are for liquid fuels, cubic feet for natural gas and short tons for coal.
questions.evidence: Kilowatthours (kWh) Electricity

questions.q: How can consumers benefit indirectly from using less electricity?
options: It reduces demand on the electric system
questions.explain: Lower peak demand can mean fewer new power plants and lower system costs.
questions.evidence: Consumers can also benefit indirectly when reducing their electricity consumption because it helps to reduce demand on the electric system.

questions.q: What does the ENERGY STAR Home Energy Yardstick do?
options: Compares a home's energy use with similar homes
questions.explain: Benchmarking shows whether a home uses more energy than it should.
questions.evidence: Home Energy Yardstick helps customers compare their home's energy use with similar homes across the country

questions.q: Which two benefits can energy efficiency and conservation bring?
options: Higher energy prices and more emissions
Lower energy bills and potentially lower greenhouse gas emissions
questions.explain: Using less energy saves money and avoids the emissions of producing it.
questions.evidence: Efficiency and conservation can help to lower consumers' energy bills and potentially reduce greenhouse gas emissions associated with energy use.

questions.q: Why do apartments use a smaller share of energy for heating and cooling than detached houses?
options: They are smaller and partly insulated by neighbouring apartments
They run only on solar power
questions.explain: Shared walls reduce heat loss and gain.
questions.evidence: Apartments are generally smaller than single-family homes, and they are often partially insulated from weather by adjacent apartments.

questions.q: How does home size relate to energy use?
options: Only the number of windows matters
Larger homes and households tend to use more energy overall
questions.explain: More space to heat and more people mean more energy.
questions.evidence: Larger homes and larger households tend to use more energy overall than smaller homes and smaller households.

questions.q: How does the commercial buildings survey (CBECS) classify buildings?
options: By the principal activity in the building
questions.explain: Offices, schools, shops and hospitals use energy very differently.
questions.evidence: CBECS includes data for energy use by type of commercial building according to the principal activity taking place in the building

questions.q: Roughly how many commercial buildings did the US have in 2018?
questions.explain: Together they had about 96.4 billion square feet of floorspace.
questions.evidence: In 2018, the United States had about 5.9 million commercial buildings

questions.q: How do some industrial facilities generate their own electricity?
options: Using residues from their processes or fuels they buy
questions.explain: On-site generation is common in energy-intensive industries.
questions.evidence: Industrial facilities also generate electricity for their own use by using residues from their industrial processes or from fuels that they purchase.

questions.q: What does the mining industry include?
options: Extracting minerals, stone and gravel, coal, oil and natural gas
questions.explain: Mining is one of the four major industrial activities in energy projections.
questions.evidence: Mining includes extracting minerals, nonmineral products such as stone and gravel, coal, oil, and natural gas.

questions.q: What does calculating your total energy consumption let you identify under ESOS?
options: Which assets or activities your route to compliance must cover
questions.explain: Total consumption is the starting point of the assessment.
questions.evidence: The calculation of total energy consumption will enable you to identify which assets or activities you will subsequently need to ensure are covered by a route to compliance.

questions.q: A fuel you use isn't in the conversion factor list. What should you do?
options: Ask your fuel provider for its properties
questions.explain: Accurate fuel properties are needed to convert usage to energy.
questions.evidence: If a fuel you use is not listed, you should contact your fuel provider to get information about its properties.

questions.q: Why might floor area figures from different sources disagree?
options: Some exclude unheated or uncooled areas while others include them
Floor area is measured in different colours
Only one source can be right
questions.explain: Be consistent about which source you use for intensity ratios.
questions.evidence: The floor area figure for some of these sources may exclude parts of the buildings which are neither heated nor cooled, whereas others may include these areas.

questions.q: Which estimation methods can you use when verifiable data is missing?
options: Direct comparison, pro-rata extrapolation and benchmarking
questions.explain: Record the method you used in your evidence pack.
questions.evidence: Some possible methods include: direct comparison pro-rata extrapolation benchmarking

questions.q: What is 'direct comparison' as an estimation method?
options: Comparing your bills with a competitor's
Using partial data to estimate complete data
questions.explain: For example, scaling up the months you have data for.
questions.evidence: This is where you use partial data to estimate complete data.

questions.q: What must participants make clear in an ESOS action plan?
options: Whether each measure is a recommendation from an energy audit
questions.explain: The plan becomes a single source for all measures and expected savings.
questions.evidence: Participants must make clear in the action plan whether the measures they include in it are recommendations from an energy audit.

questions.q: What do ESOS action plans let organisations do?
options: Set out how they are taking forward their ESOS recommendations
questions.explain: Action plans follow the notification of compliance.
questions.evidence: These enable organisations to set out how they are taking forward their ESOS recommendations.

questions.q: Who should support government departments on digital sustainability?
questions.explain: Sustainability goals should shape projects from the start.
questions.evidence: Government departments should have support from a designated digital sustainability lead.

questions.q: How does user research help make technology more sustainable?
options: It defines requirements better, so you don't buy hardware and software you don't need
It removes the need for suppliers
questions.explain: The greenest device is the one you never buy.
questions.evidence: Do your project plans include user research to more clearly define requirements and reduce the chance of buying software and hardware you do not need?

questions.q: For contracts over £5 million a year, what should a supplier have done?
options: Committed to net zero and published a Carbon Reduction Plan
questions.explain: Government procurement asks large suppliers to show their climate commitments.
questions.evidence: net zero target, and published a Carbon Reduction Plan

questions.q: Letting a non-domestic property is prohibited, unless exempt, below which EPC rating?
questions.explain: F and G rated properties need improvement or a registered exemption.
questions.evidence: There are various exemptions that apply to the prohibition on letting a property with an energy efficiency rating below E.

questions.q: When does a measure fail the '7 year payback test'?
options: When it takes more than 7 days to install
When it lasts less than 7 years
When 7 years of expected bill savings are less than its cost
questions.explain: Failing measures can support an exemption.
questions.evidence: will fail the 7 year payback test where the expected value of savings on energy bills that the measures are expected to achieve over a period of 7 years

questions.q: Who must register an exemption, and when?
options: The local council, once a year
The landlord or their agent, before relying on it
questions.explain: Exemptions go on the PRS Exemptions Register.
questions.evidence: the exemption must be registered by the landlord (or an agent for the landlord) before it can be relied on

questions.q: A property is empty and won't be let. Must the landlord improve its rating now?
options: No — only when they decide to let it again
Only if it is rated E
questions.explain: The standard applies to letting, not to owning.
questions.evidence: you don’t need to take any action to improve its rating until you decide to let it again

questions.q: Do registered exemptions pass to a new owner when a property is sold?
options: Not necessarily — they may not pass over
questions.explain: A new landlord may need to register their own exemption.
questions.evidence: may not pass over to a new owner or landlord of a property upon sale, or other transfer

questions.q: Which properties do the minimum energy efficiency regulations cover?
options: Non-domestic rented properties legally required to have an EPC
questions.explain: Properties without an EPC requirement are outside the rules.
questions.evidence: The Regulations apply to all non-domestic rented properties that are legally required to have an Energy Performance Certificate
